summary: The Companion confirms the owner's main session once at startup, so the first session file read after a restart needs one Gateway call (the file list) instead of two in a row. Only a found main session is kept; a failed or empty startup answer is not remembered, and no files RPC is ever sent without the confirmed main session.
reason: S24 07/11 19:14: release 888daa93 was rolled back because /files?scope=session was still deferred after the settle window and its late re-judgment, as on 07/11 14:05 and 05/11 23:02. Through the CLI, sessions.list took 6.5 s and a second Gateway call 3.5 s on the S24 at rest, both under one 13.5 s read deadline; right after a restart, with every acceptance read at once, the pair no longer fits.

tests.name: openclaw-plugin-mobile-ui/scripts/test-files-main-session-prewarm.cjs
tests.evidence: Captured S24 durations scaled 1/10: a cold session listing pays both calls (1005 ms); after the startup prewarm the first read needs only the file list (354 ms); a read arriving during the prewarm joins it; a Gateway down at startup and an absent main session are not remembered; no files RPC without the main session; the old build fails (no prewarm).

tests.name: test-files-http, test-file-gateway-read, test-file-gateway-limits, test-file-read-boundary, test-run-diagnostics
tests.evidence: Unchanged and green on the new build, including the R20 rule that an absent main row sends no files RPC, and the excluded server regions.

capabilities.reason: No route, method or capability change; same Gateway reads, same deadlines and same fail-closed rules.

architecture.reason: One startup call to the existing main-session lookup and its existing cache; no new store, transport or budget.

limitations: The prewarm costs one CLI Gateway call per Companion start, even if no file is read within the 10 minute cache.
The agent-scope listing still runs its three CLI calls in parallel; it settled in time on 07/11 19:14 and is unchanged here.
rollback: Revert this commit and redeploy the previous Companion.
